sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: *Olvasok* already means “I read”: the ending *-ok* says who is reading. So Hungarian does not need *én* and usually leaves it out. Say *Tanulok.*, not *Én tanulok.*

sections.title: When to say én
sections.content: Say *én* only when you stress it, to mean “I, not someone else”. *Én főzök.* means “I am the one who cooks.”

sections.title: Without and with én
rows: I am the one who reads.

items.english: I am the one who studies.

sections.content: If you put *én* in every sentence, you sound as if you were saying “me, me, me”. Keep it for the moments when you really mean “I”, not you or she.
